## AIScoreCurve

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AIScoreCurve.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

Turns one input into an amount from 0 to 1 that scales a behaviour's score: the "how much" to a condition's "whether".

Scaling spec 6.2. A straight line: `from_value` gives 0, `to_value` gives 1, with 0 below and 1 above. Set to_value below from_value to turn it round (more input, less score). A behaviour's score is `low + (max_score - low) × every curve's amount multiplied together`, where low is min_score, or 0 when min_score isn't set (`AIBehaviourBase.score()`). With no curves the score is max_score, as before.

```gdscript
target_distance, from 20 to 2     # 0 at 20 m or further, 1 at 2 m or closer: the nearer, the keener
```

### Settings and properties

- `input: String` = `""`: The input it reads, such as target_distance. See [`AIInputs`](#aiinputs).
- `from_value: float` = `0.0`: The input value that gives 0. For a time in ticks, written for 60 ticks a second.
- `to_value: float` = `1.0`: The input value that gives 1.

### Functions

- `make(input_name: StringName, zero_at: float, one_at: float) -> AIScoreCurve` *(static)*: Makes a curve in code.
- `amount(inputs: AIInputs) -> float`: The amount from 0 to 1 for this pawn's inputs now.
- `describe() -> Dictionary`: The curve as plain data, for the C++ decider, with times converted to the match's rate.
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`: Adds the slot of the input it reads to slots (as a key).

## SightGeometryFeeder

`res://assets/scripts/ai/senses/SightGeometryFeeder.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Keeps the shared SightGeometry (line of sight in C++) fed with the solid things in the scene.

With the geometry fed, line of sight can be tested off the main thread instead of with physics rays. On first use it finds every body in the tree, then follows the tree (a body entering or leaving, a collision shape added to or removed from a body); anything else the geometry notices itself, once a tick. So a designer only puts a prop on a layer in sight's sight_blocking_mask (layer 1 by default) and it blocks sight. Areas and pawns are left out. Never instanced: everything is static, so no autoload is needed. Design: scaling spec step 4.

### Settings and properties

- `enabled: bool` = `true`: Off: no geometry, so sight casts physics rays on the main thread. Read when sight is first used; set it before pawns are made.

### Functions

- `get_geometry() -> Object` *(static)*: The shared geometry, or null without the C++ library or with enabled off.

## SightSense

`res://assets/scripts/ai/senses/SightSense.gd`, extends [`AISenseBase`](#aisensebase)

Sight, for basic stealth: fills awareness of other-team pawns it can see, faster when they're close and in front.

A child of the pawn's [`AISensingManager`](#aisensingmanager). For each other-team pawn it checks, on a full pass or a refresh:

```gdscript
if there's no line of sight: no gain
gain = fill_rate Ã— ticks_since_last_check Ã— distance_factor Ã— angle_factor Ã— target.detectability
```

Ticks since the last check (capped at `max_gain_ticks`) make the checking rate not matter; the distance factor is 1 inside `near_range` and falls to 0 at `sight_range`; the angle factor is 1 in the central cone, `periphery_multiplier` in the periphery, 0 outside. Line of sight is one ray from the eyes to the target, blocked only by `sight_blocking_mask`. The eyes face where the AI is looking, else the way the body faces (where the player looks while one has the pawn). The checks run in the pawn's memory store (`AIMemoryStore` in C++, else [`AIMemoryStoreGD`](#aimemorystoregd)); with C++ the ray is tested against [`SightGeometryFeeder`](#sightgeometryfeeder)'s geometry, on worker threads when the sensing job runs. Refreshes check only the current target. Design: pawn spec 10.4, scaling spec step 4.

### Settings and properties

- `fill_rate: float` = `0.03333333333333333`: Awareness a fully visible target adds per tick: 1/30 fills it in 30 ticks, half a second. Per tick at 60 a second; at another rate it's converted to fill at the same speed.
- `near_range: float` = `8.0`: Inside this distance, in metres, distance doesn't weaken sight at all.
- `sight_range: float` = `25.0`: Beyond this distance, in metres, nothing is seen.
- `central_cone_degrees: float` = `90.0`: The width of the central cone, in degrees, where sight is at full strength.
- `periphery_degrees: float` = `160.0`: The width of everything it can see, in degrees, the central cone included. The part outside the central cone is the periphery.
- `periphery_multiplier: float` = `0.3`: How strongly the periphery sees, compared with the central cone.
- `max_gain_ticks: int` = `30`: The most ticks one check can count, so a long gap doesn't give a huge gain at once.
- `eye_height: float` = `1.6`: The height of the eyes above the pawn's feet, in metres.
- `target_height: float` = `1.0`: The height on the target the ray aims at, in metres above its feet: about the chest.
- `sight_blocking_mask: int` = `1`: Physics layers that block sight. The world, layer 1, by default.

### Functions

- `get_range() -> float`: Its `sight_range`.
- `full_pass(candidates: Pawn[], tick: int) -> void`: The whole pass runs in memory's store (C++ when available, else GDScript), with this sense's settings.
- `full_pass_prepared(job: Object, tick: int) -> void`: The full pass with the sensing job's result: the job found the candidates, how visible each is and (against SightGeometry) the line of sight, on a worker thread; this records them, the same as full_pass would. AISensingManager calls it.
- `ask_job(job: Object, reach: float, max_candidates: int) -> void`: Asks the sensing job for next tick's full pass, with where the eyes face now and this sense's settings.
- `refresh(tick: int) -> void`: Only the current target, one ray. Refreshing every remembered entity costs more than the full passes in a crowd (measured with ai_stress), and keeping a tracked target fresh is what the refresh is for.
- `visibility_of(target: Pawn) -> float`: How strongly this pawn would see the target now, before line of sight and the time factor: distance × angle × detectability. 0 when it's out of range or outside the periphery. Public so tests and debug readouts can show it.
- `has_line_of_sight(target: Pawn) -> bool`: True if nothing in sight_blocking_mask is between the eyes and the target.

## AIAwarenessState

`res://assets/scripts/ai/states/AIAwarenessState.gd`, extends [`AIStateBase`](#aistatebase)

One tunable state for every "how aware am I of an enemy" situation, such as Alert and Combat.

The default Alert and Combat are two nodes running this script with different settings, so a designer makes a new awareness state by adding a node and filling in the settings, with no code. Its prerequisites hold when the entry it looks at (the current target, or any entry in memory) meets `min_awareness`, `requires_certain` and `max_ticks_since_seen`, or separately when the pawn was hit within `hit_within_ticks` by an `attacker` of the right kind. So Combat holds when a known attacker hits, and Alert when an unknown one does (there is no damage sense). Design: pawn spec 10.6.

### Settings and properties

- `looks_at: int` = `1`: Which entries it looks at.
- `min_awareness: float` = `0.3`: Awareness it needs, 0 to 1.
- `requires_certain: bool` = `false`: On: only entries that became certain count.
- `max_ticks_since_seen: int` = `-1`: Only entries seen within this many ticks (at 60 a second) count. -1: any time.
- `hit_within_ticks: int` = `-1`: Or the pawn was hit within this many ticks (at 60 a second), by an attacker of the kind below. -1: off.
- `attacker: int` = `0`: Which attackers count for hit_within_ticks.

### Constants

- `LooksAt.CURRENT_TARGET = 0`: the target the target selector picked
- `LooksAt.ANY_ENTRY = 1`: any entry in memory
- `Attacker.ANY = 0`: any attacker
- `Attacker.KNOWN = 1`: one the pawn has in memory
- `Attacker.UNKNOWN = 2`: one it doesn't

### Functions

- `prerequisites_met(context: AIContextComponent) -> bool`

## AIIdleState

`res://assets/scripts/ai/states/AIIdleState.gd`, extends [`AIStateBase`](#aistatebase)

The state for when nothing else fits: its prerequisites always hold.

It has the lowest priority and catches every case the other states don't. Every state manager should have one, or there are moments when no state fits. Design: pawn spec 10.6.

### Functions

- `prerequisites_met(_context: AIContextComponent) -> bool`
